items.stem: Why should the OpenAI API call be made from the .NET backend rather than the React browser client?

options.text: To keep the API key secret and off the client
options.rationale: Correct: the key must stay server-side, never in the browser.

options.text: Because React cannot make HTTP requests
options.rationale: React can make requests; the issue is key exposure.
Tests are still needed regardless of where the call is made.

items.stem: How should a streaming assistant UI handle tokens as they arrive?

options.text: Render them incrementally so the user sees output immediately
Wait for the full response before showing anything
Discard tokens until the stream ends

options.rationale: The full streamed response should be rendered.

items.stem: Which TWO steps belong in getting the assistant production-ready? (Select TWO)

options.text: Add input and output guardrails on the backend
options.rationale: Correct: guardrails are part of a safe production assistant.

options.text: Add monitoring and a spend alert after deployment
options.rationale: Correct: production operation needs monitoring and cost control.

options.text: Ship the API key in the browser bundle
options.rationale: Exposing the key is a security failure.

options.text: Skip any evaluation of answer quality
options.rationale: Quality must be evaluated before and after release.

items.explanation: Correct: guardrails are part of a safe production assistant.
